items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: It was Chu, Hot Lips Paige, George Matthews on Trombone, Buster Bailey, Horace Henderson, Lawrence Lucie, Israel Crosby and you

ctx.x: No, not all that. It wasn't that. Maybe Diz had a knife in his hand, but it wasn't all that. But you know how they can build up a big story. And that was it. And Diz was fired. And the next week we were at the Apollo Theatre and Diz was sitting right up in the front row.

I guess we've kind of eased into Cab's band without trying to. Before we do that let me take it back a step to the small group records that you made, with Chu. Let's see, I'll just read off the names of the guys who were on there. Maybe that might jiggle a few memories for you. It was Chu, Hot Lips Paige, George Matthews on Trombone, Buster Bailey, Horace Henderson, Lawrence Lucie, Israel Crosby and you, and that was in 1937. You did 'Now You're Talking My Language,' 'Indiana,' 'Too Marvelous for Words,' and…

Yeah I remember them, they were all good sessions. It wasn't anything outstanding about them, but as a whole they were all good sessions, you know, and you always looked forward in doing some of Chu's records, because the sidemen that he would pick, you loved to play with.
